narrative:
The model predicted a 65% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is well above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors, ranked by importance. Your first-year grades had the strongest influence. Placing in the bottom decile of your class was substantially weaker than the average of sixth decile among accepted students, and this low performance strongly pushed the prediction toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 2.3 was the second most important factor; it sits noticeably below the 3.23 average of accepted applicants and further increased the estimated risk of failing the bar. Working full-time while in law school was the third factor. This choice actually pulled the prediction slightly toward success, yet it was not enough to offset the earlier academic signals.

Taken together, these elements led the model to conclude that the likelihood of passing the bar on the first try was too low for admission. 

To improve your chances, focus on raising your academic performance to at least the middle of your class and consider whether you can reduce work hours during law school. Strengthening these areas would directly address the factors that weighed most heavily against your application. (218 words)
